height_zero.role_in_completeness_proof: The control point lies on these nine mirrors. Exhaustion of all 82 height-zero roots proves that the strict negative direction of either witness enters the chosen finite Weyl sector; a later first-crossed mirror must therefore have x>0.

infinite_order_product.proof: A finite-order real 10 by 10 matrix has all eigenvalues on the unit circle, hence absolute trace at most 10. Here the identity-embedding trace is 10+4sqrt(2)>10.

lattice.anisotropy_derivation: If 0 != z in Q(sqrt(2))^10 had h(z,z)=0, applying the nonidentity embedding would give a nonzero isotropic vector for the certified positive-definite conjugate form. Therefore h is anisotropic over Q(sqrt(2)).

seed_C5_reversal.complete_chamber_argument: Height zero is exhaustive. Starting into its chosen Weyl sector, the first mirror on a path from the control point to the fixed witness would be a Vinberg simple wall. The equality-inclusive separator lemma bounds that wall by x<4. Every admissible positive x<4 was exhausted in the frozen Vinberg chain, and the witness is strict on all 1291 accepted walls. Thus it is regular in the complete chamber. The isometry fixes it and preserves the future cone, so it stabilizes that complete chamber.

wall_4_18_swap.complete_chamber_argument: After the exhaustive height-zero sector, any first-crossed mirror would be a positive-height Vinberg simple wall. The equality-inclusive separator lemma gives x<3, entirely inside the exhaustive Vinberg range. The midpoint is strict on every archived wall, hence regular in the complete chamber. The swap fixes it and preserves the future cone, so it stabilizes the complete chamber rather than merely the 1291-wall outer cone.
